creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 13, item 13 and batch 15, echo 1.

Every `http_get`/`http_post`/`http_put`/`http_delete` prints `Querying url: <url>` to stderr, including the query string, and a script cannot stop it per call. A script calling an API that takes its key and token as query parameters leaked both into an agent's transcript and the terminal scrollback; the token had to be rotated. Nothing flagged it until someone read the output.

```
$ rad x.rad    # http_get("https://api.example/x?key=K&token=T")
Querying url: https://api.example/x?key=K&token=T
```

Reproduces on main. The global `-q` hides the line along with `print` output, and only works after the script path, so a script can't quiet itself. `rad url:` blocks have a `quiet` option but can't send headers.

Asks: a `quiet=true` named arg on `http_*`, or silence by default with the line under `--debug`. If the line stays on by default, redact the values of query parameters named like credentials (`key`, `token`, `secret`, `password`, `sig`) so the next script doesn't leak the same way.

Where: `core/requester.go:244-246` (logs unless `quiet`); the http_* builtins never set `RequestDef.Quiet`. Main-board RAD-218 (`3d87CTcJ`) tracks the quiet half.
title: http_* log full URLs, credentials included, with no way to quiet them
